answer.evidence: The seat is 10 px wide over rows 7-12. Rows 8-10 are a light band (#d59147) that reads as the seat top seen from above. Row 11 is a darker line (#6d3b15) that acts as the front-edge line and shadow, and row 12 is the outline. Below that, the apron and legs (rows 11-15) give about 5 rows of front face. The backrest (rows 1-6, 4 px wide) is a narrow vertical post, but the seat is the main volume. The seat is thicker than the thin plank in the 'side elevation chair' reference, which is why it reads as a top surface rather than a pure profile. The call is borderline.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate chair is tiny, about 14x20 px at 2x, and uses only 6 distinct colours. The bench reference has 14 colours, the lamp 14, and the well and stall 38-40. On its wood ramp the chair shows roughly 2-3 steps: a light plank tone, a mid brown and a dark brown, with no per-plank grain and no highlight/shadow ramp. The outline is tinted dark brown (0% neutral edge pixels), so it is not a near-black sticker line, which is a point in its favour. Even so, the chair is much shallower than the bench. The bench has several wood steps, plank highlights and a shaded seat, and it is also a thin prop, so the per-tile fact is not held against the chair. By eye the chair is flat and simplified, with no texture dots or grain on the seat, back or legs. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0% only because the piece is thin. A careful artist would find it thinner and flatter than the bench next to it, so it fails.
